title: The science of sound in music
examples: How does the speed of vibration affect the sound we hear?
Can you explain the difference between pitch and volume?
What makes a high note sound different from a low note?

explain.say: Sound begins with something that moves very fast. This movement is called vibration.

draw.text: The science of sound in music

explain.say: The faster something vibrates, the higher the pitch sounds. This is related to frequency.
The number of vibrations per second is called frequency. We measure this in hertz.
Loudness is determined by how big the vibrations are. Bigger vibrations mean louder sound.
When you pluck a guitar string, the string vibrates to make sound. The way it vibrates changes the pitch.

draw.text: Guitar string vibrates to make sound.

explain.say: A real-life example is a tuning fork. When you strike it, it vibrates to create a clear, steady pitch.

draw.text: Tuning fork vibrates to set pitch.

faq.q: Why is the pitch different if I pluck a string differently?
faq.a: The pitch changes because you are changing the frequency of the vibrations. A shorter vibrating length makes the vibrations faster.
asks: What affects the pitch of a string?
How does string length change the note?

faq.q: Does the loudness depend on how fast it vibrates?
faq.a: No, loudness depends on the energy or size of the vibration, not the speed. You can vibrate slowly but very strongly.
asks: Can I have a loud, low sound?

faq.q: What is the difference between frequency and amplitude?
faq.a: Frequency is how many vibrations happen per second, measured in hertz. Amplitude relates to the size of the vibration, which controls loudness.
asks: What is the unit for frequency?
Does amplitude measure pitch or volume?

faq.q: Can sound travel through empty space?
faq.a: No, sound needs a medium, like air or water, to travel through. It cannot travel through a vacuum.

faq.q: What is the relationship between vibration and pitch?
faq.a: The relationship is direct: faster vibrations mean a higher frequency, which we perceive as a higher pitch.
asks: High pitch means fast vibration, right?

facts: Sound waves are caused by vibrations in a medium.
Pitch is determined by the frequency of the vibrations.
Loudness is determined by the amplitude of the vibrations.
Frequency is measured in hertz, or Hz.

quiz.say: A very low, deep note is produced by:
quiz.why: Low pitch means the vibrations are slow, and if it is also loud, the vibrations must be large in size.

wrong.0: This would create a high, very loud sound.
wrong.1: This would create a low, quiet sound.
wrong.3: This would create a high, quiet sound.

quiz.say: If a sound has a high frequency but is very quiet, what is happening?
quiz.why: High frequency means the vibrations are fast, while small amplitude means the vibrations are not very big.

wrong.0: This would be a high, very loud sound.
wrong.1: This would be a low, very loud sound.
wrong.3: This would be a low, quiet sound.

quiz.say: A sound that is deep and booming, but not too loud, is best described by:
quiz.why: Deep sounds have low frequency, and 'medium' amplitude means it is neither too loud nor too quiet.

wrong.0: This would be a high-pitched sound of medium volume.
wrong.1: This would be a low, quiet sound.
wrong.2: This would be a high, quiet sound.
